html:
The Kok Narr were an Aboriginal Australian people of the southwestern Cape York Peninsula, on the coastal plains of the Gulf of Carpentaria in Queensland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

They are known mainly through their language, Kok Narr, a Paman language of the Pama-Nyungan family that is now extinct. Little else is recorded. Neighbours on the map include the Kokoberra, the Kurtjar and the Kunjen. Cattle stations spread over this country from the late 1800s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
